summary: Harker is admitted to Castle Dracula by an old white-moustached man in black who proves to be the Count himself, welcoming him with the ritual words 'Enter freely and of your own will'. He is given a fire-lit supper and a bedroom reached through a windowless octagonal room; the Count does not eat. By day Harker finds a gold-served breakfast, no servants, no mirrors, and a library of English books on England. The Count asks him to stay and correct his English, explains the blue flames as marking hidden treasure, and finalises the purchase of Carfax at Purfleet, which Harker describes from his notes; an atlas ringed at London, Exeter and Whitby. On 8 May Harker shaves with a small mirror, cannot see the Count's reflection, is almost attacked when he bleeds, and the Count recoils from the crucifix and throws the mirror into the courtyard. Exploring, Harker finds every door locked, and concludes the castle is a prison.

scenes.title: Waiting at the great door
scenes.location: Castle courtyard and great studded door
scenes.summary: Harker, dazed, stands before a worn carved stone doorway with no bell or knocker and reflects on being a newly qualified solicitor.
scenes.key_quote: Of bell or knocker there was no sign

scenes.title: The Count opens the door
scenes.location: Entry hall and passage of Castle Dracula
scenes.summary: Chains, bolts and a long-unused key; an old man in black with an antique silver lamp invites him to enter of his own will, grips his hand with icy strength, and carries his luggage up the winding stair.
scenes.key_quote: Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!

scenes.title: Supper by the fire
scenes.summary: Harker hands over Mr. Hawkins's letter, eats roast chicken, cheese, salad and old Tokay, smokes a cigar; the Count does not eat. Harker studies the Count's features, notices hairy palms, long pointed nails, rank breath and a wave of nausea. Wolves howl and the Count calls them children of the night.
scenes.key_quote: Listen to them—the children of the night. What music they make!

scenes.title: Day in the empty castle; the library
scenes.time: 7 May, between five and six o'clock
scenes.summary: Harker finds a cold breakfast and a note, gold table service, no mirrors, no servants, no bell. In the library he finds English books; the Count enters and asks Harker to teach him English intonation, permits him to roam except behind locked doors.
scenes.key_quote: You may go anywhere you wish in the castle, except where the doors are locked

scenes.title: Blue flames explained
scenes.summary: The Count explains blue flames mark hidden treasure on one night a year, and tells how patriots hid treasure in the soil fought over by Wallachian, Saxon and Turk.
scenes.key_quote: a blue flame is seen over any place where treasure has been concealed

scenes.title: The Carfax purchase
scenes.summary: Plans and deeds are signed; Harker reads aloud his description of Carfax at Purfleet. The Count approves of the old chapel and gloom. Harker finds an atlas with rings at London, Exeter and Whitby. Cockcrow ends the evening.
scenes.key_quote: I am glad that it is old and big.

scenes.title: The shaving glass
scenes.summary: Count appears behind Harker without reflection; Harker cuts himself, the Count lunges at his throat, touches the crucifix cord and changes; he hurls the mirror from the window.
scenes.key_quote: But there was no reflection of him in the mirror!

scenes.title: Discovering the prison
scenes.location: Castle stairs, south room with precipice view
scenes.summary: Harker explores, sees a thousand-foot drop and endless forest from a south room, and finds every door locked and bolted.
scenes.key_quote: The castle is a veritable prison, and I am a prisoner!

locations.name: Castle courtyard
locations.description: Large courtyard with several dark ways leading from it under great round arches.
locations.quote: several dark ways led from it under great round arches

locations.name: Great door
locations.description: Old door studded with large iron nails in a projecting doorway of massive worn carved stone; no bell or knocker; secured with chains, bolts and a key.
locations.quote: a great door, old and studded with large iron nails, and set in a projecting doorway of massive stone

locations.name: Entry passage and winding stair
locations.description: Stone passage, great winding stair and another passage where footsteps ring on stone floor.
locations.quote: up a great winding stair, and along another great passage, on whose stone floor our steps rang heavily

locations.name: Dining room
locations.description: Well-lit room with table set for supper and a mighty hearth with a great log fire; later laid with breakfast with coffee kept hot on the hearth.
locations.quote: a table was spread for supper, and on whose mighty hearth a great fire of logs, freshly replenished, flamed and flared

locations.name: Octagonal room
locations.description: Small octagonal room between the dining room and the bedroom, lit by a single lamp, apparently without any window.
locations.quote: a small octagonal room lit by a single lamp, and seemingly without a window of any sort

locations.name: Harker's bedroom
locations.description: Great bedroom with log fire, centuries-old costly hangings; window opens to the courtyard; no mirror.
locations.quote: the hangings of my bed are of the costliest and most beautiful fabrics

locations.name: Library
locations.description: Room full of English books and periodicals; a central table covered with magazines; lamps lit at dusk; sofa; atlas.
features: London Directory, Red and Blue books, Whitaker's Almanac, Army and Navy Lists, Law List
locations.quote: a vast number of English books, whole shelves full of them

locations.name: Locked door opposite Harker's door
locations.description: A door Harker tries and finds locked.
locations.quote: The door opposite mine I tried, but found it locked.

locations.name: South room at the precipice
locations.description: Room off the stairs facing south, the castle on the very edge of a precipice with a drop of a thousand feet and a sea of green tree-tops with silver rivers in gorges.
features: view of forest and river gorges
locations.quote: A stone falling from the window would fall a thousand feet without touching anything!

locations.name: Carfax (described)
locations.description: Estate at Purfleet with a high old stone wall, rusted oak and iron gates, twenty acres, dark pond fed by springs, large straggling house of all periods including a thick-walled keep with a few high barred windows, next to an old chapel; near a private lunatic asylum.
features: stone keep with barred high windows
locations.quote: The estate is called Carfax, no doubt a corruption of the old Quatre Face

characters.name: Count Dracula
characters.appearance: tall old man; strong aquiline face, high thin nose with arched nostrils, lofty domed forehead, scanty hair at temples, profuse elsewhere; massive eyebrows nearly meeting; cruel-looking fixed mouth under heavy moustache; sharp white protruding teeth; remarkably ruddy lips; pale pointed ears; broad strong chin; extraordinary pallor; broad coarse hands with squat fingers, hair in the palms, long fine pointed nails; ice-cold; rank breath
characters.clothing: black from head to foot without a speck of colour
characters.personality: courtly, controlling, proud of his lineage, eager to blend into England
characters.speech_style: excellent but stilted English with strange intonation; puts patronymic first
notable_lines: Welcome to my house! Enter freely and of your own will!
I am Dracula; and I bid you welcome, Mr. Harker, to my house.
Here I am noble; I am boyar

objects.name: Antique silver lamp

objects.quote: an antique silver lamp, in which the flame burned without chimney or globe of any kind

objects.name: Great door with chains, bolts, key
objects.description: Studded door with rattling chains, massive bolts and a key turned with the loud grating noise of long disuse.
objects.quote: A key was turned with the loud grating noise of long disuse

objects.name: Mr. Hawkins's sealed letter

objects.quote: I can send a sufficient substitute, one in whom I have every possible confidence.

objects.name: Gold table service

objects.quote: The table service is of gold, and so beautifully wrought that it must be of immense value.

objects.name: Roast chicken, cheese, salad and old Tokay

creatures.name: Count Dracula

vampire_lore.rule: Must be invited to enter, of free will
vampire_lore.detail: The Count ritually invites Harker to enter freely; he does not step forward until Harker has crossed the threshold.
vampire_lore.quote: Enter freely and of your own will!

vampire_lore.detail: His handshake is cold as the dead and crushing.
vampire_lore.quote: more like the hand of a dead than a living man

vampire_lore.rule: Does not eat, drink or smoke
vampire_lore.detail: He claims to have dined; Harker later notes he has never seen him eat or drink.
No image in the shaving glass.
vampire_lore.quote: The whole room behind me was displayed; but there was no sign of a man in it, except myself.

vampire_lore.detail: No mirror anywhere, not even a toilet glass.
vampire_lore.quote: in none of the rooms is there a mirror

vampire_lore.detail: On seeing Harker's cut he lunges at his throat.
vampire_lore.quote: his eyes blazed with a sort of demoniac fury

vampire_lore.detail: Touching the crucifix's cord instantly ends his fury.
vampire_lore.quote: It made an instant change in him

vampire_lore.rule: Dawn and cock-crow end his night
vampire_lore.detail: The crow of a cock makes him spring up and leave quickly.
vampire_lore.quote: Count Dracula, jumping to his feet

vampire_lore.rule: Physical tells: hairy palms, pointed nails and ears, rank breath, canine teeth
vampire_lore.quote: there were hairs in the centre of the palm

vampire_lore.detail: The Count is always absent in the afternoon and Harker does not see him by daylight.

Listen to them—the children of the night.

puzzles.name: No reflection
puzzles.setup: Harker shaves with a hand mirror.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker turns around and sees him but not in the glass; he notices blood.
puzzles.game_idea: Detection mini-game: use a mirror to identify who in a room is a vampire.
puzzles.quote: But there was no reflection of him in the mirror!

puzzles.name: The castle of locked doors
puzzles.obstacle: Every door locked or bolted; the great door key is missing.
puzzles.book_solution: Not solved; Harker only finds a south room with a view.
puzzles.game_idea: Maze of locked doors with key-hunting across later chapters; safe vs unsafe areas.
puzzles.quote: doors, doors, doors everywhere, and all locked and bolted

puzzles.name: Finding a bell and servants
puzzles.setup: Look for a way to call the servants.
puzzles.book_solution: Harker infers the Count does everything himself.
puzzles.game_idea: Observation puzzle collecting clues that the castle is empty (no bell, no mirror, no servants, fresh logs).
puzzles.quote: I looked for a bell, so that I might let the servants know I had finished; but I could not find one.

puzzles.name: Reading Dracula's atlas
puzzles.book_solution: Harker notes London east, Exeter, Whitby.
puzzles.game_idea: Clue item that reveals future-chapter locations.
puzzles.quote: on examining these I noticed that one was near London on the east side

combat.name: Throat grab over the cut
combat.tactics: Harker evades; the crucifix breaks the Count's frenzy.
combat.outcome: Count recovers, destroys the mirror, leaves.
combat.game_idea: Quick-time/turn event: bleeding raises the enemy's frenzy; using the crucifix cancels the attack.
